chunk_findings.detail: `remove_owned` resolves the target for the containment check but then deletes the resolved path instead of the requested target. If `target` is a symbolic link inside `root` pointing to another directory inside `root`, the function deletes the linked directory and leaves the symlink dangling. For example, with `root = tmp_path / "owned"`, `important = root / "important"`, and `link = root / "link"` symlinked to `important`, `remove_owned(link, root)` passes the checks and calls `shutil.rmtree(resolved)`, removing `important` while `link` still exists. The requested cleanup of `link` fails and an unrelated owned directory is destroyed; the safety check should use the resolved path, but deletion should be performed on `target` or symlinks should be refused.
chunk_findings.title: tests/safe_cleanup.py:25

chunk_findings.detail: The cleanup passes `tempfile.gettempdir()` as the “owned root” to `remove_owned`. Since `remove_owned` is exercised by `tests/test_safe_cleanup.py` as removing any directory strictly inside the supplied owned root, this treats the entire system temp directory as owned by this test. For example, if `report.diagnostics` is `/tmp/other-test/diag.json`, the finally block removes `/tmp/other-test`, a directory this test did not create. If the test’s CWD happens to be under the system temp directory, e.g. `/tmp/ci/repo`, and `report.diagnostics` is `/tmp/ci/repo/diag.json`, the cleanup removes the CWD. The empty-diagnostics guard prevents the original `Path("").parent` case, but the root is still too broad; the owned root should be the specific temp directory created by this run, not the whole system temp dir.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_upgrade_dry_run_diagnostics.py:344

chunk_findings.detail: `remove_owned(s.path, tempfile.gettempdir())` uses the whole system temp directory as the “owned root”. This is not a directory the test owns, so the new safety guard still permits deleting any absolute path under `/tmp` (for example `/tmp/other-tests/important`) if `s.path` ever resolved there. It also makes the test fail in a valid pytest environment where `--basetemp` is outside `tempfile.gettempdir()` (concretely `pytest --basetemp=$PWD/.pytest-tmp` with default `TMPDIR=/tmp`); then `s.path` is not under `/tmp`, `remove_owned` raises `ValueError`, and this test fails where the old `shutil.rmtree` worked.

chunk_findings.detail: `remove_owned` validates the target but not the owned root. `Path(root).resolve()` silently turns an empty or relative root into the current working directory or an ancestor, so an absolute target can pass the “strictly inside root” check even though the test does not own that directory. For example, with the current working directory `/repo`, `remove_owned("/repo/subdir", "")` deletes `/repo/subdir`, and `remove_owned("/repo", "..")` deletes `/repo` itself because `root` resolves to `/` and `/repo` is a child of `/`. This is the same class of bug the change is meant to prevent: an empty/relative value derived from the test can make cleanup delete the repository.
chunk_findings.title: tests/safe_cleanup.py:21

chunk_findings.detail: `remove_owned(s.path, tempfile.gettempdir())` gives the cleanup helper the system-wide temporary directory as the “owned” root, instead of the actual test-owned root. On a run such as `pytest tests/test_tree_lifecycle.py --basetemp=/workspace/.pytest` with `TMPDIR=/tmp`, the suite’s `repo` fixture is created under `/workspace/.pytest`, so `W.scratch_tree(repo, "side")` returns a path under that custom basetemp, not under `/tmp`. `remove_owned` then computes `/tmp` as the base, finds `/tmp` is not in `s.path.resolve().parents`, and raises `ValueError`, causing this test to fail even though the product code is correct.

chunk_findings.detail: `base = Path(root).resolve()` still accepts an empty or relative root. With the current working directory `/repo`, `remove_owned("/repo/subdir", "")` resolves the root to `/repo`, sees `/repo/subdir` as strictly inside it, and deletes `/repo/subdir`; `remove_owned("/repo", "..")` resolves the root to `/` and deletes `/repo` itself. The previous HIGH finding’s root-validation part is therefore still present; the new symlink/parent-resolved containment does not reject an empty or relative “owned” root.
chunk_findings.title: tests/safe_cleanup.py:21

chunk_findings.detail: The new containment expression `resolved = path.parent.resolve() / path.name` leaves the final path component unresolved, so a target ending in `..` bypasses the “strictly inside root” check. For example, with root `/repo/owned` and target `/repo/owned/..`, `path.parent.resolve()` is `/repo/owned` and `path.name` is `..`, so `resolved` is `/repo/owned/..`; `base` `/repo/owned` is in `resolved.parents`, the guard passes, `path.is_symlink()` is false, and `shutil.rmtree(path)` deletes `/repo`, the parent of the supposedly owned root.
chunk_findings.title: tests/safe_cleanup.py:22

chunk_findings.detail: The non-symlink branch calls `shutil.rmtree(path, ignore_errors=True)` without `follow_symlinks=False`, so symlinks inside the deleted tree are followed. Given root `/tmp/owned` and target `/tmp/owned/d` containing a symlink `out` to `[REDACTED:path]`, `remove_owned` recurses through `out` and deletes `[REDACTED:path]`, even though the target is supposed to be confined to the owned root. The new top-level `path.is_symlink()` branch protects only the final component, not symlinks nested inside the tree.
chunk_findings.title: tests/safe_cleanup.py:28

chunk_findings.detail: The `root` argument is still not validated: `base = Path(root).resolve()` turns an empty or relative root into CWD or an ancestor. With CWD `/repo`, `remove_owned("/repo/subdir", "")` passes the containment check and `shutil.rmtree("/repo/subdir")` deletes the directory, even though `""` owns nothing. The symlink-following change in this commit does not address this input.

chunk_findings.detail: The added `monkeypatch.setattr(tempfile, "tempdir", str(sysdir))` does not guard the cleanup when `report.diagnostics` is empty. On the exact regression this change is supposed to fix, `report.diagnostics == ""`, and the existing `finally` still executes `shutil.rmtree(Path("").parent)`, i.e. `shutil.rmtree(".")`, deleting the current repository. Giving `tempfile` a safe tempdir only changes the non-empty case; it does not prevent the empty-diagnostics deletion.

chunk_findings.detail: `remove_owned` resolves the `root` argument before checking containment, so a symlinked `root` makes the helper treat the symlink target as the owned root and permits deletion outside the test’s owned directory. For example, with `root = tmp_path / "link"` symlinked to `/outside` and `target = root / "sub"` (a real directory under `/outside`), the target string is absolute and contains no `..`; `base = Path(root).resolve()` becomes `/outside`, `resolved` becomes `/outside/sub`, and `base in resolved.parents` is true. Since `target` itself is not a symlink, `shutil.rmtree(path, ignore_errors=True)` follows the root symlink and removes `/outside/sub`, which the test does not own. The guard should refuse a symlinked root (or otherwise avoid resolving `root` into an unowned target) before allowing deletion.
chunk_findings.title: tests/safe_cleanup.py:22

chunk_findings.detail: The safety check and the deletion are separate operations: the validation resolves `path.parent`, but then the original `path` is passed to `shutil.rmtree`. Interleaving defeats the only guarantee: root is `/tmp/owned`, target is `/tmp/owned/a/b` where `a` is currently a real directory. After line 25 validates `/tmp/owned/a/b` as inside the root but before line 31 runs, another process renames `/tmp/owned/a` and creates `/tmp/owned/a` as a symlink to `/tmp/victim`. `shutil.rmtree('/tmp/owned/a/b')` then follows the new symlink `a` and deletes `/tmp/victim/b`, outside the owned root. The helper advertises that it cannot delete what the test does not own, so this is a promise the code does not keep.
chunk_findings.title: tests/safe_cleanup.py:25-31 (remove_owned)

chunk_findings.detail: `shutil.rmtree(path, ignore_errors=True)` silently swallows a missing target. In `test_install_twice_then_uninstall_unsets_and_a_missing_dir_still_restores`, the old `shutil.rmtree(GH.hook_dir(wt))` would raise `FileNotFoundError` if `GH.install(wt)` regressed and did not create the hook directory, failing the test. `remove_owned` returns normally in that case, so the test can pass even though the directory to remove was never created; the regression it relied on to create that missing-directory state is no longer detected.
chunk_findings.title: tests/safe_cleanup.py:31 (remove_owned)

chunk_findings.detail: The `.` case is vacuous for the bug it claims to cover. The fixture makes `cwd` a sibling of `owned` (`cwd = tmp_path / "cwd"`, `owned = tmp_path / "owned"`), so `remove_owned(".", owned)` would be rejected by a simple “target must be under owned” guard even if the helper had no special-case for `""`/`"."`: the resolved target is `tmp_path/cwd`, which is outside `owned`. To actually exercise the Be5e7dc7e27 failure, the test should `chdir` into a directory below `owned` and then call `remove_owned(".", owned)` and assert that cwd survives; otherwise an implementation with only a containment check still passes all parameterized cases but would delete the current directory when the cwd lies inside the owned root.
